rationale: Evidence: across iterations 0 and 2, 0 of 60 development trials finished. Every run ended off track, with progress of only 0.04 to 0.12 and max error pinned just past the 0.06 m limit. RMS error is about 0.03 m on every track, and steering oscillation is low (about 0.07), so the controller is not jittering. The robot departs the line early and fast, at nearly the same point regardless of gain changes. Because progress barely moved across three different gain sets, gain alone is not the limiting factor. Speed is the most likely cause: at base_speed 1.3 to 1.6 the robot carries too much momentum into the bends and overshoots the 6 cm limit before the sensors can correct. Completion is worth 500 points and the time term is worth at most 60, so staying on the line matters far more than finishing fast. The off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4), which stays at 0.06 for any body width up to about 0.18, so widening the body does not help. Changes: (1) base_speed lowered from 1.3 to 0.9 so the robot has time to correct at each bend; (2) kp held at 4.0 and ki at 0.5, the iteration 2 values, to isolate the speed effect; (3) kd kept at 0.6 for damping; (4) sensor geometry, wheel track, body and mass unchanged, so the speed change is the only variable. Expected result: the robot should hold the line through the bends and reach progress well above 0.12. Completion is possible but may take longer than 3 s, which trades some time points for the much larger completion bonus. If the robot still leaves the line at 0.9, the next race should point to the sensor footprint or the gains.
